messages.subject: integrating non-conversion rate
parts:
Hi Altuna,
I included lambda DNA to calculate non-conversion rate during bisulfite treatment. I have non-conversion rates for each libraries (lets say, library A1- 4%, A2 - 0.3% and library B1-0.8%, B2-0.9%). Obviously there is a big difference in conversion rates. Is there someway methylkit takes account for non-conversion rate? Or is there other applications which I can use for this purpose?
 
Thanks in advance.

Milan

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] integrating non-conversion rate
parts:
Thinking about this, if you accept this naive approach you may be able to do this in an easy way. 

Assume conversion rate for a sample is the probability of a converted C is really a C. Then, you can multiply the conversion rate per sample with number of Cs (numCs) and (round it to the nearest integer) to get an expected number of correctly converted Cs. 

This can be done using reconstruct() function, where you need to get first a percent methylation matrix (there is a function for that), correct it by multiplying it with the sample conversion rates (each column is a sample), then use reconstruct to get the corrected counts.

best,
altuna
